name: opencode-wait
tagline: Near-Zero-CPU waiting for OpenCode agents on HPC login nodes
description:
A maintained fork of the opencode-wait plugin that lets OpenCode agents pause without burning CPU. It combines a near-zero-CPU HTTP listener, sentinel-file watching and kernel-level sleeps so an agent can wait for a Slurm job, a remote completion signal or a new user message on an HPC login node without tripping cgroup or runaway-process watchdogs.

The fork adds HTTP wake-up with token authentication and payload return, sentinel-file completion with optional content read and cleanup, abort-controller cancellation, live progress metadata and predictable per-session ports. The upstream timer-based plugin is preserved, and the fork is released as v0.2.0.
purpose: To let coding agents wait for long-running external jobs without polling, burning CPU or being killed by login-node watchdogs.
strengths: Consumes virtually no measurable CPU while waiting by using epoll/inotify and true kernel sleep
Opens a predictable per-session port (40000 + hash(sessionID) % 4096) with token authentication
Accepts a simple curl wake-up from a compute node and returns exit codes or results to the model
Watches sentinel files on NFS/Lustre and can read or delete their content on completion
Cancels the wait and frees sockets immediately through OpenCode's abort controller
Reports a live progress bar, elapsed and remaining time, and the bound port
Preserves the upstream timer-based wait while adding the new wake-up paths
limitations: Linux-specific: relies on epoll/inotify and will not run unchanged on macOS or Windows
HTTP wake-up requires network reachability from the compute node to the login node
The repository carries upstream history and is maintained as a fork, not a clean-room implementation
There is no separate UI beyond OpenCode's metadata bar
installation:
# Install the plugin in OpenCode
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-wait"]
}

# Or build from source
bun install
bun run build
usage:
# Ask OpenCode to wait for a Slurm job
{
  "seconds": 3600,
  "reason": "Waiting for Slurm job 5251529",
  "port": "auto"
}

# Wake the waiting session from the job script
curl -s -X POST "http://${OPENCODE_HOST}:${OPENCODE_PORT}/wake" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"token\":\"${OPENCODE_SESSION}\",\"exitCode\":0}"
roadmap: Keep the fork synchronized with upstream releases
Add more completion transports for batch systems beyond HTTP and sentinel files
Improve portability beyond Linux where the underlying primitives allow it
